title: May-to-July growth raised linear September Antarctic ice forecast error after July extent and year in 2004-2024
abstract: We tested whether May-to-July Antarctic sea ice extent growth improved September forecasts after July extent and year were included. Expanding linear fits used earlier years from 1989 and gave 21 test forecasts for 2004-2024. Adding growth raised mean squared error by 12.5%. Root mean squared error rose from 0.407 to 0.432 million square kilometres. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for MSE reduction was -32.9% to -0.6%. A one-year block interval included zero. All five full-period model comparisons had higher point error with growth. The primary loss remained without 2023 in scoring and after removal of one day with reported missing area. This is a conditional forecast test, not a test of a physical recovery mechanism. The short record, changing conditions, current data version and loss-resampling assumptions limit inference. Original code, aggregate scores, audits, a figure, exact source hashes and external-data regeneration instructions are included.

display.caption: Adding growth raised forecast error in all five full-period model comparisons. Intervals use three-year blocks of fixed forecast losses. Source: Sea Ice Index Version 4, NSIDC.
